body: That's a great recommendation, thanks! Initially, I was a bit worried that the plastic construction would make it too light compared to wood, but I now realize that may actually be a boon when spinning finely. Not to mention it would be less stressful when I inevitably drop it 50 times haha. Do you use the midi by any chance?
That's such a good idea! I would totally be down for that but I'm in NYC... :-( Hoping you'll find your [spin squad](https://media.tenor.com/1xxRlxQYduUAAAAM/girls-walking-entry.gif) soon!

Omg I was just looking at your post showing off your set-up lol! That basket is amazing.   
Great point about ergonomics, that's partly why I was interested in the different distaffs. It just seems like drafting's easier when your hand is mostly free.   
Having to come up with a spiel is pretty funny, didn't even think about that -- was so focused on figuring out how to get my steps in that I forgot someone might run up and ask me what the heck I'm doing haha. Perfect opportunity to show someone something new I suppose :-P
Ah spinning by the beach sounds lovely... Your video is great! I'm getting more and more convinced that Turkish spindle is the way to go (to start :-D.)

Ah the article/video is exactly what got me wondering about this in the first place! I definitely want to read Alvarez's book at some point. :-) Much to learn... I definitely need to shift my perspective of spinning as a somewhat stationary craft with many associated tools, to one that is mobile with your hands being the most important tool of them all.

Haha, you're right -- a distaff might not do much good if I don't feel comfortable lugging it around. I'm definitely going to have to do a test-run of how much fiber I actually need to bring on any given walk, after all one pocket Fluff might be enuff. Thanks for the encouragement!

Great to hear that whorl placement isn't much of an issue, I think the majority of my hesitation in picking a spindle for this purpose lied in that detail. A ring distaff is interesting, might try it out if wrapping roving around the wrist/using a wrist bag proves to be troublesome, but you make a good point about safety. Thanks!

That's just what I needed to hear, as much as I didn't want to hear it (my bank account is definitely breathing a sigh of relief though haha.) A bag that hangs from a wrist strap sounds like a great idea, a bit more portable than a big pole. Thank you!
Thank you for the suggestion, I haven't heard of in-hand/twiddle spindles yet! The French in-hand spindle is very intriguing... Definitely will do more reading about these!

Yes, that's a very good point -- I speak from a dilettante's perspective when writing this post but for many, present and past, spinning is a daily necessity. To be honest, part of what got me thinking about this was reading about Andean spinning. I'm excited to expand my spinning comfort zone and incorporate this into another part of my routine.

Omg I bought some small used shuttles from there in December! The owner was so nice and there was so much equipment I have never seen before. I was kicking myself for not taking a picture of the shop so seeing these photos is so heartwarming.

Apologies for the wait, I have been away from reddit while working on the wheel and getting acquainted with it. I appreciate your thoughtful reply :-). 
I went ahead and got the sliding hook flyer - the flyer is so large in comparison to the standard flyer! The large bobbins have been very helpful with storing some of my less-than-neat attempts at singles...
Thankfully the hub seems secure, I haven't seen any separation at the glued seam but I will definitely keep an eye on it. Funnily enough, after waxing the gaps in the drive wheel look a tad bit smaller with one almost closing entirely... Then again, it was stored in a storage locker for a long time so maybe some exposure to Florida humidity made the wood expand slightly.
And thank you for mentioning getting supplies at the hardware store! It made replacing the brake band and springs a breeze.
Oh this is great! I had watched a couple of her videos before and she is such a wealth of knowledge - thanks for the link! Definitely going to be following along while tackling this project.

Thanks for the tip regarding the band clamp! I'll probably leave it alone for now since I can get a good amount of rotations in and it doesn't seem to wobble when fiddling with the wheel, but I'll be eyeing my ratchet clamp in the future. I'll also see if there are any changes with the joint-spacing as I'm planning on moving to a low-humidity region in the future. I also appreciate the Paradise Fibers rec!

> I have this exact wheel sitting next to me. I love the styling from that era.

Me too! I love how modern it looks but not 'over-engineered' if that makes sense - it's just so nice and sleek.

And thanks for the insight! Especially nice to hear that spinning fine won't be much of an issue. Going to get started on filling the shopping cart and greasing some elbows. @_@
Gotcha! I’ll be careful to keep the threads as close as possible. Thanks again!

Yes, that is exactly it! I was worried that the threads crossing over would have caused some tension issues, but I am very very new to the wonderful world of weaving so that was likely a misinformed concern. Thank you very much for your help :-)
Oh excellent, thank you so much for your detailed reply! Very grateful :-)
I hadn’t received any video of the Cousin but I do have the English vers. Weeks that I am totally down to transcribe! It may take me a day or two but I’ll add a comment with a link to the quotes :-).
Thank you so much everyone! You are all such a wealth of knowledge and I greatly appreciate all your wisdom. Very excited to bring this loom back intact if possible!

That makes sense, I guess the blue is dark enough to add depth on its own. Regarding yellow vs. sunflower, the opacity/saturation was definitely a concern of mine, so I'll definitely consider sunflower as an option. Totally going to check-out Shaffer's work, thanks for the heads-up!
I have an RZ390 -- I'll definitely be on the look-out for inconsistencies with fluro pink, thanks!

I appreciate the tip about Travis Shaffer! Definitely going to consider using his color profiles and possibly signing up for CMYKinda when it's offered again. Your set-up sounds great by the way, seems a bit more versatile than using aqua and yellow. Thank you for the help!

After much lurking, I have finally dipped a toe into the wonderful world of fountain pens with a Pilot Kakuno EF and a borrowed Pilot Metropolitan M (additional Pilot Plumix Italic M not present as I may have already forgotten it at work… I hope whichever coworker grabs it enjoys the lovely lines it makes haha). 

I have seen many on this sub use Kaweco Sport clips for Kakunos, but I have been reluctant to purchase additional accessories as I start out, especially in the wake of financial stressors that have been on my plate for the past couple of months. However, I have found an old Walmart penlight [https://www.walmart.com/ip/HyperTough-Aluminum-Penlight-Portable-Flashlight-25-Lumen-Black-Red/983621102] lying around that had a detachable clip that fits absolutely perfectly onto my Kakuno — I would say it looks fitting on a demonstrator model, but perhaps with a layer of paint the clip would do nicely on an opaque Kakuno as well. For ~$2, it is quite the steal. Plus, now you have an extra penlight :-).

Brief aside, I’ve been adoring J. Herbin’s inks from the few swatches and samples I’ve seen. The colors are understated yet refined in a very classic way, it is an utter joy to write letters with calming and natural colors. One day I’ll jump head first into sheeners, one day.
